transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Thanks for sending the draft contract, Mr Dawson. I've read it carefully, and there are a few points I'd like to discuss.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Of course. Please call me Greg. What's on your mind?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: First, the fee. The contract says four thousand pounds for the complete website, but the brief has grown since we first talked. You now want an online shop as well, and that's a significant extra.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: I see your point. What would you consider fair?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: I'd suggest six thousand, with the shop included. I've worked out that the shop alone is about forty hours of work.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: That's more than I budgeted. The most I could go to is five thousand five hundred.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Let's think about payment terms, which might help us meet in the middle. If you're able to pay thirty per cent upfront rather than on completion, I could accept five thousand eight hundred.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Hmm. A third at the start seems reasonable. Let's say thirty per cent upfront, forty per cent on delivery of the design, and the rest when the site goes live. And I'd want a fixed price at five thousand eight hundred.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: That works for me. Now, the next point is ownership. The draft says you'll own everything I produce, including my templates and code that I've developed for other clients.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: We always include that clause. I need to be sure the site belongs to us.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: I understand, but I can't transfer ownership of tools I've built over years. I'd propose that you own the finished website and its content, while I keep the right to reuse general components.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: That sounds reasonable. I'll check with our lawyer, but I don't foresee a problem.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Third, the deadline. The contract says delivery by the first of March. Given the extra work, I'd prefer the fifteenth. I also have to allow time for your feedback. In my experience, clients take longer than expected to respond.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: Fair comment. Our marketing team is busy in February. If I promise to give feedback within three working days, can you keep to March first?

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: If feedback comes within three days and there are no more than two rounds of changes, yes. Additional rounds would be charged at fifty pounds an hour.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Finally, cancellation. The draft lets you cancel at any time without payment. That's risky for me, because I'd have done work I couldn't be paid for. I'd like a clause saying I'm paid for the work done up to the date of cancellation.

transcript.speaker: S2
transcript.text: That seems only fair. I'll ask for the contract to be amended and send it to you tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Thank you, Greg. I'm looking forward to working together.
